approved: Sex Discrimination Amendment (Boosting Superannuation for Women) Bill 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would let companies pay more into the retirement savings of female staff without breaking sex discrimination rules.
It would add a new part to the Sex Discrimination Act 1984 so that employers do not need a special exemption to make these extra payments.
The explanatory memorandum notes that in 2011–12, average superannuation balances were $82,615 for men and $44,866 for women.
Employers could boost superannuation for women employees without violating the Sex Discrimination Act 1984.
The bill would remove the requirement for employers to apply for an exemption under section 44 of the Act to make higher contributions for women.
It would insert a new section into the Act to permit this practice.
Employers and women employees covered by the Sex Discrimination Act 1984.

Introduced the Greens' Sex Discrimination Amendment (Boosting Superannuation for Women) Bill 2014, citing a persistent 17 per cent gender pay gap that leaves Australia ranked 24th of 142 countries for women's equality, and noted 2011-12 figures showing average superannuation balances of $82,615 for men compared with just $44,866 for women.
